headline: Back-to-back ultra-distance days on foot at controlled HR — the durability quality this block trains, confirmed in the clearest terms yet. The engine held its shape across both. Recovery is now the story.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The two trail days sit at the centre of everything right now: consecutive very long efforts at low, disciplined HR, exactly the back-to-back durability signature flagged as worth confirming — and it's landed. The recent four-week running block has stepped up sharply over the prior block, driven almost entirely by these two days rather than a broad lift across all sessions. Strength has gone quiet through the crossing window, which is expected and not a concern given the year-to-date base. Steps remain very high and essentially flat across training and rest days — a large, consistent background load that never really switches off. The cardio-load status still reads detraining, which is a rolling-average artefact lagging behind two days that were anything but; expect it to flip. Sleep through the crossing has been short and broken, which matters for how much these days cost rather than for what they demonstrate.
sections.trends: Year-to-date volume is running far ahead of last year at this point, and the 16-week shape is a genuine build rather than noise — the recent four weeks meaningfully outweigh the prior four. That said, the shape is being pulled hard by two outlier days, so the underlying weekly rhythm is less steep than the headline change suggests. This fits the standing philosophy well: durable year-round capacity with the willingness to absorb a large discrete effort when it appears, rather than strict linear periodisation. Nothing here reads as plateau or drift.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and the HR it sits at are unchanged from the baseline, last tested early July — no new data point has moved it, and the crossing days wouldn't be expected to, since sustained low-HR ultra work doesn't refresh a threshold marker. The current aerobic picture is best read as banked and stable rather than sharpening; the recent training has developed the durability end of the range, not the top end. If you want confirmation the fast engine is intact, that will come from a threshold or tempo session once you're recovered, not from these.
sections.zones: The zone distribution over the crossing is almost entirely Z1 with a thin sliver of Z2 across both very long days — textbook time-on-feet intensity, and appropriate for what those days were for. This is not grey-zone drift; it's deliberate low-intensity durability work, and the per-session shapes confirm both days held that discipline for their full duration without creeping up. The only genuinely mixed session in recent memory was a short earlier run with real Z4 time, which is a different tool entirely. For the current phase, the distribution is doing exactly what it should.
sections.hr_comparison: Nothing stands out as anomalous. The strength sessions with HR data sit in the expected low-to-moderate band for functional work, and where run HR came from the fallback source the values track sensibly against neighbouring sessions rather than diverging. No source-agreement concern worth acting on.
sections.calendar: The running streak continues to hold at its all-time length, and the calendar shows the pattern shift you'd expect around a big effort: a cluster of short Copenhagen runs, then the two large trail days, with strength dropping out through the crossing window. The interesting thing to watch is what fills the days immediately after — whether normal frequency resumes cleanly or there's a deliberate gap while the effort is absorbed. Consistency remains the strongest structural feature of this athlete's log.
sections.personal_bests: None of the current standing PBs are the target of this phase — the short-distance and half bests date from last autumn's speed window and aren't in reach off ultra-durability training. The 50K best, set on the 137 km day, is conceptually closest to what's being trained now; whether these back-to-back days translate into an improved long-distance mark depends on a measured effort rather than these controlled ones. No PB is realistically imminent from the current block.

watch_items: Watch whether the cardio-load status flips out of detraining now that both long days are logged — a slow flip signals a heavier real cost than the low HR implied.
Watch the first few easy runs after the crossing for elevated HR at normal pace, which would show the effort is still being paid down.
Watch whether nightly sleep consolidates now that the crossing window is closing, since recent nights have been short and fragmented.
Watch when strength re-enters the log — its return is a fair marker that the trail block has been absorbed and normal training rhythm has resumed.
